text:
1. Johnson did not wish to praise Shakespeare by the standards of his own age.
2. Johnson distrusted the praise that any single age bestows.
3. Fashion admires what flatters it.
4. One generation may value a writer for reasons the next generation finds trivial or cannot understand.
5. Johnson accepted duration as the only valid test of a literary work's worth.
6. A work that has been read and valued through many changes of manners and opinion owes its hold to something more than the accident of its first reception.
7. Johnson held that by the test of duration, Shakespeare's standing was already settled.
8. At the time of Johnson's judgment, Shakespeare had been dead for about a century and a half.
9. Between Shakespeare's death and Johnson's time, the English language had changed.
10. Between Shakespeare's death and Johnson's time, the stage had changed.
11. Between Shakespeare's death and Johnson's time, critical taste had shifted from one doctrine to another.
12. In Johnson's time, Shakespeare's plays were still acted, read, and quoted.
13. Shakespeare's plays were valued by people who knew nothing of the circumstances that first produced them.
14. Johnson wrote that the stream of time continually washes away the dissoluble works of other poets but passes without injury by the adamant of Shakespeare.
15. The poets who shared Shakespeare's stage had faded from esteem over time.
16. Shakespeare's reputation had not faded over time.
